newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian cable TV network launches internet service.
newsitem.headline: Belgian cable TV network launches internet service.

text.p: Belgian group Telenet launched its "Pandora" Internet service on Friday, the first of a series of products for Belgium's northern region of Flanders.
"This is Telenet's entry on the information highway," chief executive officer Paul Van der Spiegel told a news conference.
Through its telecommunications network Telenet wants to reach 60,000 households by the end of 1997, 500,000 by end-1998, fully covering Dutch-language Flanders by late 2002, he said.
Telenet is converting existing cable infrastructure -- which reaches 97 percent of the population -- into an interactive broadband network designed for a wide range of services.

Van der Spiegel said Telenet, partly owned by U S West Media Group's U S West International and Flanders' government investment company GIMV, might also offer internet directly on TV in the longer term.
"Technically it's already feasible, it might be done within the next two years," he told Reuters.

Roland Siebelink, Telenet's internet project manager, said Pandora, which operates through the high-capacity television cable, would be much faster than existing lines, and allow full multi-media use.
Audio quality would be superior and Pandora could also offer interactive video.
The internet package, including connection, modem rental and help desk support, would cost 10,000 francs ($260) and the monthly fee would be 1,500 francs.
Van der Spiegel said Telenet was also conducting trials for telephone traffic through the cable network and had held its first phone conversation last month.
A survey showed that 41 percent of the calls were of better quality than those of traditional phone calls, he said.

Van der Spiegel foresaw a deal with state telecommunications operator Belgacom on links between the two networks. "We expect full agreement on interconnection before the end of December." He declined to elaborate on the price-setting.
Telenet was holding talks with Mobistar, the operator of Belgium's second GSM mobile phone network. He declined to give details.
Telenet's network will cost 47 billion francs, of which 37 billion will be paid by the Telenet partners and 10 billion by the cable companies directly.
Telenet has a workforce of 100 which will be gradually rise to about 600 in 2002.
